steps: Local event starts from current physical time.
Logical counter breaks ties when physical time does not advance.
Receiver merges local, physical, and received timestamp components.
Result preserves causality while staying close to wall time.

lesson.scenario: Two database nodes preserve causal timestamp order despite wall-clock regression and concurrent physical times.
entities: Events ordered by HLC and node ID

steps.title: Timestamp a local event
steps.narration: A sets HLC to (1700000100000,0) because wall time exceeds its prior physical component.

nodeB.detail: No work accepted in this phase

hlcB.detail: No work accepted in this phase

register.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: The event receives a compact mostly-physical timestamp.
steps.invariant: Each tick is lexicographically greater than the node previous HLC and every receive is greater than the transmitted HLC; physical time may regress, and equal concurrent HLC values require a stable external tie-breaker.

steps.title: Advance on causal receipt
steps.narration: B receives a1 when its wall clock is 1700000099980; it takes max(local physical,remote physical,wall) and increments logical to one.
action: Send a1 timestamp with replication message

register.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: The receive timestamp is greater than the send timestamp despite slower wall time.
steps.invariant: Each tick is lexicographically greater than the node previous HLC and every receive is greater than the transmitted HLC; physical time may regress, and equal concurrent HLC values require a stable external tie-breaker.

steps.title: Survive wall-clock regression
steps.narration: Because wall time is below the stored physical component, B keeps 1700000100000 and increments logical from one to two.
action: Tick after wall moves back to 1700000099000

register.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.invariant: Each tick is lexicographically greater than the node previous HLC and every receive is greater than the transmitted HLC; physical time may regress, and equal concurrent HLC values require a stable external tie-breaker.

steps.title: Merge the returned causality
steps.narration: A receives b2 at wall 1700000100000, sees equal physical maxima, and advances logical above max(0,2) to three.

register.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: The causal chain a1 -> b2 -> receive is strictly ordered.
steps.invariant: Each tick is lexicographically greater than the node previous HLC and every receive is greater than the transmitted HLC; physical time may regress, and equal concurrent HLC values require a stable external tie-breaker.

steps.title: Resolve equal timestamps deterministically
steps.narration: Concurrent updates at HLC (1700000100200,0) tie on both HLC fields, so the register uses node ID B as a final deterministic tie-breaker.
action: Compare HLC then immutable node ID
steps.outcome: All replicas choose the same value without claiming the tie was causal.
steps.invariant: Each tick is lexicographically greater than the node previous HLC and every receive is greater than the transmitted HLC; physical time may regress, and equal concurrent HLC values require a stable external tie-breaker.

production.scenario: A fintech ledger spans Virginia, Frankfurt, and Singapore, and every balance mutation needs globally comparable commit order without trusting pure wall time.
components: global payment services issuing debit and credit mutations for merchant traffic
service boundary that validates idempotency keys and ledger invariants before commit
control-plane service that uses hybrid logical clocks to preserve causality while staying close to wall-clock order
durable authority in CockroachDB for account journals, balances, and commit timestamps
serves account projections and audit exports from stable committed ledger history
control path that quarantines skewed regions and replays suspect ranges for audit
observability path for clock skew, commit inversion alerts, and replay outcomes
flows: Payment services submit idempotent journal mutations from multiple regions at once.
Before commit the API asks the HLC service for a timestamp that preserves causal ordering.
The authoritative ledger stores the mutation with its HLC timestamp and consensus metadata.
Readers materialize balances and exports from the durable journal in commit order.
Reconciliation can force a region into safer behavior when its physical clock drift grows risky.
The durable ledger feeds targeted audit scans for any interval touched by skew or failover.
Dashboards expose clock skew, commit wait inflation, and detected ordering anomalies.
